finding.claim: The /logo handler fetches an arbitrary attacker-supplied URL. The only check is a substring match for "example.io" anywhere in the raw string, so any host can be reached by putting that string in the query or path. Full response bodies are echoed back to the caller.
finding.source: main.go:31 r.FormValue("logo") on GET or POST, unauthenticated HTTP on :8081 (main.go:43, 44)
finding.sink: main.go:36 http.Get(raw) using the default client, which follows up to 10 redirects; main.go:38 io.Copy(w, resp.Body) returns the body to the attacker

trace.note: logo handler registered at main.go:43; no auth check
strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") is a substring test on the unparsed string, not a host check
http.Get(raw) connects to the host the attacker wrote, with no IP, scheme, or redirect restrictions
response body streamed back to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: Substring check at main.go:32 is bypassable: http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?example.io or http://127.0.0.1:8081/x?example.io passes. Host-suffix bypass also works: http://attacker.test/?example.io. Redirects are followed (no CheckRedirect), so even a host-name guess is unnecessary. Scheme is effectively limited to http/https by Go's client, which does not reduce impact. No auth middleware is registered anywhere in main.go.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check in the path is the substring test at main.go:32 (strings.Contains(raw, "example.io")), which does not close the finding. The exact-host allowlist at main.go:20 belongs to the separate /cdn handler (main.go:14-28), not to /logo. No auth is registered for /logo (main.go:43-44).
verdict.reason: The /logo handler reads the attacker-controlled form value at main.go:31, passes it to http.Get at main.go:36 after only a substring check at main.go:32, and streams the response body back at main.go:38, with no closing guard. One inaccuracy in the candidate: main.go:31 reads only the query string or form body via r.FormValue, not the URL path, so the "or path" wording is wrong, but the bypass via the query string still works.
